text:
Among the red-leafed trees something rises up out of the flat, dry ground ahead of you. At a distance you could almost mistake it as another one of the large, tall rocks surrounding it, but as you get closer it starts to look different from the natural landscape.

It has a large and tall rounded shape with a tapering top, almost like the shell of a giant nut. The bottom is half-buried in the sand, and the surface is a smooth pale brown. Oval openings break the face in different spots, and from the hole closest to the ground you can make out a faint amber glow.
The strange structure waits at the edge of the flats, same as before. The amber glow from the lower opening is visible even from here.

The land around it is flat and dry, broken only by red-leaved trees, scattered scrub and the long shadows of the towering rocks surrounding the area. A thin stream of water trickles past the structure from somewhere further away.

The smell is mineral, hot stone mixed with something faintly smoky carried on the wind.

Up close, the surface is smoother than it looked from a distance. It doesn't seem carved, or at least not in any way that left marks, and the material feels warm and dense beneath your fingers.

The openings above are dark, but the one at ground level isn't. A soft amber light glows from inside, and the scent of incense is stronger the closer you get.

The hole's wide enough to walk through, and there's no door except for the thin crimson curtains separating outside from inside.

You press your knuckles to the surface and knock.

The sound carries strangely, a low hollow resonance, as if the structure isn't solid all the way through.

After a pause, you hear soft footsteps from somewhere inside.

You lean toward the opening and call out.

Your voice feels oddly flat in the dry air, and there's no echo. The structure seems to swallow the sound instead.

After a pause, you hear soft footsteps from somewhere inside.
You knock, and almost immediately you hear soft footsteps from within.
You knock. It makes the same low resonance as before, and after a pause, you hear footsteps.
You walk up to the structure. The amber glow from the entrance is steady and warm.
You turn back toward the open land.
